reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports nano-twinning and heterogeneous grain structures enhancing strength and ductility in specific fcc medium-entropy alloys (CrCoNi), but none of the passages address the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, its caloric phase transformation, or the proposed thermomechanical processing route. E3 is a simulation study on nanoimprinting of AlxCoCrFeNi, unrelated to the alloy or processing method. Thus, the key premises linking the intervention to this specific alloy and its caloric performance lack direct prior evidence.
premises: Warm rolling at 300–350 °C and sub-transus annealing at 500–550 °C can induce a heterogeneous microstructure with nano-twins and ultrafine grains in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Nano-twins and ultrafine grains enhance mechanical integrity (toughness, ductility, crack resistance) in high-entropy alloys.
Twin boundaries facilitate reversible reorientation under applied fields/pressures, preserving the caloric phase transformation.
The processing parameters (temperature, time) can be controlled to avoid unintended phase modifications that would degrade caloric performance.
